:::{#exm-epe-split-noise}
#### The two pMSEs differ by the noise variance

Take a population whose mean function is known:
$\Outvar \mid \Predvar = \predvar \sim \ndist{\sin(2 \pi \predvar), \varpar}$ with $\sdpar = 0.3$.
Fix $\predvar = 0.25$, where $\truemeanfnf{\predvar} = 1$,
and fit a cubic polynomial by least squares to $\nobs = 30$ observations.
We draw $5{,}000$ training sets,
each with its own new outcome at $\predvar$,
and average the squared errors of the two targets over them.

```{r}
#| label: epe-split-noise-sim
#| code-fold: false
split_x0 <- 0.25
split_reps <- 5000
split_sigma <- 0.3
split_truth <- function(x) sin(2 * pi * x)
split_draw <- function(n) {
  x <- stats::runif(n)
  tibble::tibble(x = x, y = split_truth(x) + stats::rnorm(n, sd = split_sigma))
}

set.seed(2)
split_errors <- purrr::map(seq_len(split_reps), \(i) {
  train <- split_draw(30)
  fit <- predict(lm(y ~ poly(x, 3), data = train), tibble::tibble(x = split_x0))
  new_y <- split_truth(split_x0) + stats::rnorm(1, sd = split_sigma)
  tibble::tibble(
    new_outcome = (new_y - fit)^2,
    mean_estimate = (split_truth(split_x0) - fit)^2
  )
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()

split_pmse <- colMeans(split_errors)
```

The pMSE of the prediction of the new outcome is
`r sprintf("%.3f", split_pmse[["new_outcome"]])`.
The pMSE of the prediction as an estimate of the mean is
`r sprintf("%.3f", split_pmse[["mean_estimate"]])`.
Their difference, `r sprintf("%.3f", split_pmse[["new_outcome"]] - split_pmse[["mean_estimate"]])`,
is close to $\varpar =$ `r sprintf("%.2f", split_sigma^2)`,
as @thm-epe-split-noise says.
It is not exactly equal because $5{,}000$ training sets give only a Monte Carlo approximation to each expectation.

:::
